questions.q: According to a report published on 15 October 2026, what is the purpose of the special voter-enrolment drives planned in Meghalaya after 26 October?
o: To help eligible voters missing from electoral rolls enrol
questions.e:
Correct answer: To help eligible voters missing from electoral rolls enrol.
Key points: The 15 October report says election authorities in Meghalaya and other regions are organising enrolment drives for eligible people whose names are absent from the electoral roll. The date matters because the report places the camps after the scheduled final-roll publication on 26 October; confirm later official notices before acting on the schedule.
Why the other options are incorrect: The report concerns voter registration, not driving licences, municipal tax collection or school examinations.
Exam takeaway: Electoral rolls are prepared under election law; eligible citizens should check their enrolment status and use the prescribed application process.
Source: https://m.economictimes.com/news/india/boost-your-voting-rights-sikkim-meghalaya-and-ladakh-launch-major-voter-enrollment-campaigns/articleshow/134970107.cms

questions.q: A report published on 15 October 2026 stated that India's direct-tax collections after refunds, as of 14 October, had reached approximately:
questions.e:
Correct answer: ₹13.38 lakh crore.
Key points: Financial Express reported net direct-tax collections of ₹13.38 lakh crore after refunds as of 14 October 2026, up 13.2% year on year. The same report gave ₹16.03 lakh crore before refunds; that is a different measure. It also reported securities transaction tax separately.
Why the other options are incorrect: ₹16.03 lakh crore was the pre-refund figure, ₹6.92 lakh crore referred to non-corporate tax after refunds, and ₹46,840 crore was the reported securities transaction tax amount.
Exam takeaway: Always distinguish gross collections from collections after refunds and distinguish direct tax from securities transaction tax.
Source: https://www.financialexpress.com/money/income-tax-direct-tax-mop-up-rises-13-stt-revenues-surge-52-4362271/

questions.q: What name was given to the planned AI foundation model for physics announced by CERN and Mistral AI on 15 October 2026?
questions.e:
Correct answer: Flare.
Key points: Reuters reported that CERN and Mistral AI announced a long-term partnership to develop an AI foundation model for scientific discovery, initially focused on collider physics. The planned system is to be trained on simulated particle-collision data rather than ordinary text alone.
Why the other options are incorrect: Atlas and Hadron are associated with particle-physics terminology and experiments, but they are not the name reported for this planned model; QuarkNet is not the announced model name.
Exam takeaway: Connect the organisation (CERN), partner (Mistral AI), model name (Flare) and intended field (physics research).
Source: https://www.reuters.com/science/cern-mistral-partner-build-ai-foundation-models-physics-2026-10-15/

questions.q: According to Reuters on 15 October 2026, how many runs did West Indies captain Shai Hope score not out in the fourth T20 International against India?
questions.e:
Correct answer: 102 not out.
Key points: Reuters reported that Shai Hope made an unbeaten 102 in the fourth T20 International in Hyderabad, helping West Indies level the series. A score described as 'not out' means the batter was still at the crease when the innings ended.
Why the other options are incorrect: The figures 88, 76 and 121 do not match the innings reported in that match report.
Exam takeaway: For sports current affairs, retain the player, opponent, format, venue/date and key performance together; verify subsequent match results separately.
Source: https://www.reuters.com/sports/cricket/windies-hope-worried-about-excess-baggage-after-landing-another-player-match-2026-10-15/

questions.q: According to Meghalaya Tourism, which traditional rule is associated with the Mawphlang Sacred Grove?
o: Visitors may collect medicinal plants freely
Nothing should be taken from the grove, not even a twig
Trees may be cut with a visitor permit
questions.e:
Correct answer: Nothing should be taken from the grove, not even a twig.
Key points: Meghalaya Tourism describes Mawphlang as a sacred grove protected through Khasi customs and traditions. The prohibition on removing natural objects reflects the community's cultural and ecological stewardship of the forest.
Why the other options are incorrect: Free collection, removal of stones or routine tree-cutting contradict the stated customary restriction.
Exam takeaway: Sacred groves are examples of community-based biodiversity conservation and the relationship between cultural traditions and forest protection.
Source: https://www.meghalayatourism.in/explore/destinations/by-interest/sacred-groves-%26-forest-sanctuaries/mawphlang/

questions.q: Meghalaya Tourism describes the David Scott Trail as a route of approximately 16 km between which places?
questions.e:
Correct answer: Mawphlang and Lad Mawphlang.
Key points: Meghalaya Tourism describes the trail as an old route of about 16 km between Mawphlang and Lad Mawphlang in the Khasi Hills. It is associated with colonial-era travel routes as well as local landscapes and heritage.
Why the other options are incorrect: The other pairs are different places in Meghalaya and are not the endpoints given in the official tourism description.
Exam takeaway: Learn major Meghalaya destinations with their region, nearby town and distinctive cultural or geographical feature.
Source: https://www.meghalayatourism.in/explore/destinations/by-region/khasi-hills/david-scott-trail/

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.e:
Correct answer: Article 148.
Key points: Article 148 provides for the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India. The CAG is a constitutional authority whose audit role supports legislative oversight of public finances.
Why the other options are incorrect: Article 280 concerns the Finance Commission; Article 324 concerns the Election Commission's election-related powers; Article 356 concerns failure of constitutional machinery in a State.
Exam takeaway: Memorise constitutional bodies alongside their establishing Articles and primary functions.
Source: https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/359f70a69695affb9d72f8393102bd2e.pdf

questions.q: Article 123 of the Constitution empowers the President to promulgate an ordinance when:
o: Circumstances require immediate action while both Houses are not simultaneously in session, subject to constitutional limits
questions.e:
Correct answer: Immediate action is required while both Houses are not simultaneously in session, subject to constitutional limits.
Key points: Article 123 provides the President's ordinance-making power when the constitutional conditions are met and immediate action is considered necessary. An ordinance has temporary legislative force and must be laid before Parliament when it reassembles; it is not an unlimited substitute for legislation.
Why the other options are incorrect: Permanent dissolution alone is not the full constitutional test; the Supreme Court does not trigger the power by request; a Governor's resignation is unrelated.
Exam takeaway: Learn Article 123 for the President and Article 213 for a Governor's ordinance power, noting their distinct constitutional settings.
Source: https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/359f70a69695affb9d72f8393102bd2e.pdf

questions.q: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal, introduced in 1793, is most closely associated with which Governor-General?
questions.e:
Correct answer: Lord Cornwallis.
Key points: The Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal in 1793 under Lord Cornwallis. It fixed the land-revenue demand payable by zamindars to the East India Company, while its social and economic effects on cultivators and intermediaries remain important themes in colonial history.
Why the other options are incorrect: Warren Hastings preceded Cornwallis in the relevant period; Wellesley and Dalhousie served later and are associated with other colonial policies.
Exam takeaway: Link the Permanent Settlement with 1793, Cornwallis, Bengal and the zamindari revenue arrangement.
Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Permanent-Settlement

questions.q: Which longitude is used as India's Standard Meridian for Indian Standard Time?
questions.e:
Correct answer: 82°30′ E.
Key points: Indian Standard Time is based on the 82°30′ east longitude, which is taken as the Standard Meridian of India. Longitude is measured east or west of the Prime Meridian; degrees north or south describe latitude.
Why the other options are incorrect: 68°7′ E and 97°25′ E are longitudes but are not the designated Standard Meridian; 23°30′ N is a latitude, not a longitude.
Exam takeaway: Do not confuse the Standard Meridian (82°30′ E) with the Tropic of Cancer (about 23°30′ N).
Source: https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iess101.pdf
questions.source: NCERT, Contemporary India-I, India: Size and Location

questions.q: The policy repo rate is best described as the rate at which:
o: The RBI pays interest on all household savings accounts
The RBI provides short-term liquidity to eligible participants against approved collateral under repo operations
Commercial banks lend directly to the Union Government
questions.e:
Correct answer: The RBI provides liquidity to eligible participants against approved collateral under repo operations.
Key points: The repo rate is a key monetary-policy rate associated with RBI liquidity operations. Changes can influence money-market rates and, through transmission, borrowing and deposit rates in the wider economy.
Why the other options are incorrect: The repo rate is not a universal household savings-deposit rate, is not the rate for commercial-bank lending to the Union Government, and has no direct connection to tax collection.
Exam takeaway: Distinguish the repo rate from the reverse repo rate, standing deposit facility rate, bank rate and retail deposit rates.
Source: https://systemhealth.rbi.org.in/Scripts/FS_Overview2752.aspx.html
questions.source: Reserve Bank of India, monetary-policy instruments

questions.q: Complete the sentence: “The officer is responsible ___ maintaining the register.”
questions.e:
Correct answer: for.
Key points: The standard construction is “responsible for” followed by a noun or gerund. “Responsible to” usually identifies the authority to whom someone is answerable; “at” and “with” do not fit this construction.
Why the other options are incorrect: “to” changes the meaning to accountability to a person or authority; “at” and “with” are not used in this phrase.
Exam takeaway: Learn prepositions as collocations and check the grammatical role of the phrase.
Source: Cambridge Dictionary — https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/

Correct answer: 210.
Step-by-step solution:
1. Convert each percentage to a fraction or decimal: 20% = 20/100 = 0.20 and 15% = 15/100 = 0.15.
2. Calculate 20% of 750: (20/100) × 750 = 150.
3. Calculate 15% of 400: (15/100) × 400 = 60.
4. Add the results: 150 + 60 = 210.
Why the other options are incorrect: 190, 200 and 220 do not equal the sum of the two correctly calculated percentages.
Exam takeaway: For a sum of percentages of different numbers, calculate each part separately and add only at the end. Shortcut: 20% is one-fifth; 15% is 10% + 5%.

questions.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 4:7 and their sum is 99. What is the smaller number?
questions.e:
Correct answer: 36.
Step-by-step solution:
1. Let the numbers be 4x and 7x.
2. Their sum is 4x + 7x = 99, so 11x = 99.
3. Divide both sides by 11: x = 99 ÷ 11 = 9.
4. The smaller number is 4x = 4 × 9 = 36; the larger is 7 × 9 = 63. Check: 36 + 63 = 99 and 36:63 simplifies to 4:7.
Why the other options are incorrect: 27 and 32 do not produce the required 4:7 ratio with a partner summing to 99; 63 is the larger number, not the smaller one.
Exam takeaway: Add ratio parts first, divide the total by that sum, then multiply by the part for the requested quantity.
questions.verificationStatus: concept-checked; original practice; arithmetic independently checked

Key points: Examine the successive differences: 8 − 3 = 5; 15 − 8 = 7; 24 − 15 = 9; 35 − 24 = 11. The differences are consecutive odd numbers increasing by 2, so the next difference is 13.
Calculation: 35 + 13 = 48.
Why the other options are incorrect: 46 would add 11, repeating the previous difference; 50 and 52 would require differences of 15 and 17, skipping the expected 13.
Exam takeaway: For number-series questions, first compare differences, then second differences or multiplication patterns before selecting an answer.

questions.q: In which atmospheric layer is most of the ozone layer concentrated?
questions.e:
Correct answer: Stratosphere.
Key points: Most atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere, where it absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation. Ozone also occurs near the ground in the troposphere, where it is a pollutant, so location matters.
Why the other options are incorrect: The troposphere is the lowest weather layer; the mesosphere lies above the stratosphere; the thermosphere is much higher and is not where most atmospheric ozone resides.
Exam takeaway: Distinguish protective stratospheric ozone from ground-level ozone pollution.
Source: https://scied.ucar.edu/learning-zone/atmosphere/ozone-layer

questions.q: Rule 138 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules primarily deals with:
o: Information to be furnished before movement of goods and generation of an e-way bill
Refund of accumulated input tax credit only
questions.e:
Correct answer: Information before movement of goods and generation of an e-way bill.
Key points: Rule 138 of the CGST Rules sets out the information and procedure for generating an e-way bill before the movement of covered goods. The rule contains conditions, exceptions and later amendments, so officers should consult the current text for a specific case.
Why the other options are incorrect: Input-tax-credit eligibility is governed mainly by the CGST Act and related rules; refund procedures and composition-scheme eligibility are addressed elsewhere.
Exam takeaway: For GST administration, identify the correct Act section or rule and always check the latest amended text before applying a threshold or exception.
Source: https://cbic-gst.gov.in/pdf/10112020_CGST-Rules-2017_Part-A_Rules.pdf
